How much does a Grok Imagine video cost?

Edited by Emmanuel Gonzalez

Some links on this page are affiliate links. Affiliate disclosure.

On the official API, Grok Imagine Video 1.5 starts at $0.02/s for grok-imagine-video-1.5-lite at 480p (xAI API pricing, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT). A clip is billed per second of output, for 1 to 15 seconds, so a 5-second lite 480p video is $0.10 and a 15-second clip is $0.30, before any input-image charge. Paid Grok plans that include video generation draw from a shared weekly usage pool; those pages do not publish a credits-per-video figure, so this guide does not invent one. Affiliate links never change this price order.

Last checked 2026-11-13.

Related: Grok Imagine Video 1.5 model page · cheapest AI video generator by model · credit calculator.

How much does a Grok Imagine video cost?

The cheapest published rate in the catalog is $0.02/s on xAI API (480p, grok-imagine-video-1.5-lite), checked Nov 13, 2026 PT. That is a pay-as-you-go API rate: one video costs that figure times the output length, plus any stated input charge. On paid Grok plans that include video generation, usage comes from a weekly pool shown as a percentage; the official pages do not say how many credits one video uses, so no plan dollars-per-second figure is shown.

How much is one Grok Imagine video on the official API?

Official output rates, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT on the API pricing page: grok-imagine-video-1.5 is $0.08/s at 480p, $0.14/s at 720p, and $0.25/s at 1080p; grok-imagine-video-1.5-lite is $0.02/s at 480p, $0.03/s at 720p, and $0.14/s at 1080p. Clips are 1 to 15 seconds, and cost scales with duration. Image input is $0.01 per image on both models. On grok-imagine-video-1.5, preset-voice audio input is free. Lite 1080p is upscaled from 720p; 1.5 is native 1080p. Sources: API pricing, video overview, 1.5 model page, and 1.5 lite model page, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT.

Do X Premium or SuperGrok plans include video, and what are the limits?

On the official plan page, video generation is not included on Free or Plus, and is included on Premium, Super, Ultra, Teams, and Enterprise. Plus does include image generation (Imagine). Super's card also says you can create 1080p, 15-second videos. Paid usage is a single weekly pool shared across Grok products, not a daily cap per product. The pool is shown as a percentage; the official pages do not publish the absolute size of the pool or a credits-per-video figure. There is a 720p cap per tier: 720p videos automatically fall back to 480p once that cap is hit, but the numeric cap is not stated. Extra usage credits can be bought on the web from $5, expire one year after purchase unless otherwise stated, and are priced at standard rates, which the FAQ says is higher than included weekly usage. Sources: x.ai/pricing feature grid and plan cards; X plan list prices (Plus $8/mo or $80/yr, Premium $30/mo or $300/yr, Super $100/mo or $1,000/yr, Ultra $200/mo or $2,000/yr; prices exclude tax); Grok FAQ on the weekly pool, Extra Usage Credits, and the 720p fallback; usage limits and extra usage credits, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT.

Existing Cursor, SuperGrok, and X Premium plans continue unless you change or cancel them. New self-serve customers choose the current plan names on x.ai/pricing. Paid plans include API access, but API usage is billed separately at standard model rates and does not draw from the plan's usage pool (same pricing-page FAQ, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT).

Which route is cheapest for a typical video?

For a short text-to-video clip with no input image, the cheapest published 480p and 720p rates are lite at $0.02/s and $0.03/s on the official API, matching Runway's lite credits at those resolutions. The cheapest published 1080p rate is lite at $0.14/s; the official video overview says that 1080p lite output is upscaled from 720p. If you need native 1080p, references, or voice references, grok-imagine-video-1.5 is $0.08/$0.14/$0.25 per second at 480p/720p/1080p on the official API and on fal. A paid Premium-or-higher plan can be cheaper per clip only if you stay inside the included weekly pool, but this guide cannot convert that pool into dollars per second because the official pages do not give the numbers.

  • Casual short clips, no references: official lite or Runway lite at the same output $/s, watching input-image add-ons on Runway and the official $0.01/image fee.
  • Native 1080p, references, or voices: official 1.5 or fal at the official 1.5 rates; Runway 1.5 costs more per second.
  • Included plan usage: only Premium and higher include video generation. This can be the cheapest route if you stay inside the weekly pool, but the official pages do not say how many videos that pool buys.
  • After the weekly pool is used up: Extra usage credits are at standard rates, which the FAQ says are higher than included usage. The official API at list price is the rate those “standard rates” can be compared with, but the FAQ does not print a credits-per-video table.

Affiliate links never change this price order.

Hidden costs

Input media. Official 1.5 and lite charge $0.01 per input image. 1.5 also charges for video input; preset-voice audio input is free. Runway adds 1 credit ($0.01) per image or audio reference on 1.5, and 1 credit for an image-to-video start frame on lite. fal's text-to-video page says no per-image charges apply on that endpoint.

Failed generations. The official pricing, FAQ, and vendor pages checked today do not state a single refund rule for a failed Grok Imagine video. Treat that cost as unknown.

Plan pool and 720p fallback. A high-quality video uses more of the weekly pool than a chat message, but the amount is not published. After the 720p cap for your tier, 720p output falls back to 480p. Extra credits expire after one year unless otherwise stated, and can only be bought on the web today.

Older official model. grok-imagine-video (without 1.5) is a separate official model at $0.05/s at 480p and $0.07/s at 720p, with $0.01 per second of video input and $0.002 per input image, and no 1080p rate on the pricing table (grok-imagine-video model page and API pricing, checked Nov 12, 2026 PT). It is not this catalog model and is not mixed into the 1.5 tables.

What is confirmed, and what is not

Confirmed Nov 12, 2026 PT on official xAI pages: the 1.5 and 1.5-lite output rates and image-input fee; 1–15 second duration; lite 1080p upscaled from 720p; preset-voice audio input free on 1.5; batch video at standard rates; plan prices and the feature grid for video generation (not on Free or Plus; included from Premium up); weekly shared usage pool replacing per-product daily limits; Extra Usage Credits from $5, one-year expiry unless otherwise stated, priced at standard rates; 720p fallback after an unstated per-tier cap; API usage on paid plans billed separately; existing SuperGrok and X Premium plans continue unless changed.

Confirmed on vendor pages today, matching or adding to the catalog: fal 1.5 output rates and 5-second examples; Runway 1.5 and lite credit rates, including lite 1080p at 14 credits/s; Atlas standard T2V rates matching the official list; Replicate's $0.08/s I2V billing with no resolution breakdown; Krea's approximate 1.5 counts; Magnific's per-image Grok credit line.

Unknown: how many credits or dollars one Imagine video uses on a paid plan; the size of each plan's weekly pool and of the 720p cap; whether a US-regional 1.1× token premium applies to Imagine video; a failed-generation refund rule; a Higgsfield 1.5 video rate; a Replicate resolution breakdown; Krea or Magnific video dollars-per-second. Invented figures are not shown for those gaps.

How do we calculate this?

Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page (https://vidfare.com/about/).
